answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn a history of completed jobs before its votes or reputation carry weight. A Sybil attacker must then split capital across many identities, keep each funded, and perform real work long enough to build credibility; one nebula of forged accounts cannot cheaply amplify influence. If caught cheating, the stake is slashed, making a plume of disposable identities costly rather than free to forge.
